title: I Took the Archery-Lane Timer to the Coach Who Camped Our Numbered Target

parts.text: I nocked on lane three at 6:03 p.m. and coach Vela was already shooting our numbered target. The light said: ONE LANE. FORTY MINUTES. TARGET STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-one, club member, holding a scorecard that listed our ends. Vela shrugged. "Coaches are the lane." I photographed the light, the booking, and her arrows in our gold. Then I asked for the lane log. At 6:11 the range pinged why Vela's name was on our forty. I kept my voice range-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A light is only a light until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The range can see Vela's arrows in our gold during our booking.

social.video_title: She shot our numbered target on our lane — Part 1/2
social.description: Archery lane, a coach in our gold, a forty-minute light she posted. I logged the arrows. Would you have asked for the lane log?

parts.text: Vela called it a sight-in until the range asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the light, and the arrows still. The target went back to our face. Vela ran her own forty and told the next coach atmosphere was always about grouping. Grouping is a word coaches use when a booking exists. Lane policy now has a second line: COACHES ARE NOT THE LANE. I keep our card on a labeled clip. Vela brown-bags her jokes. The range finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Lane log, numbered target, and a second line on the light. Was a sight-in ever our gold?
